title: Henan rural-bank depositors' New Year's Day march and Zhengzhou petition
location: Highway routes toward Zhengzhou, Henan; RFA separately reports depositors petitioned at the Zhengzhou banking-and-insurance regulator. Exact sites and route are unknown.
scope: Reported Henan depositor mobilization toward Zhengzhou; whether the highway march and regulator petition were one gathering, multiple arrivals, or separate episodes remains unresolved.
organizer: Unknown. NTD and RFA cite social-media/video material but do not identify an event organizer.
participants_original: NTD describes 大批 (a large number/group) of depositors; RFA says 不少人 (many). Neither gives a count.
threshold_50_evidence: The reports describe a large group/many depositors traveling and petitioning, but provide no number. RFA states it could not independently verify the messages/videos. No numeric bound is inferred; the 50-person threshold remains unresolved.

start_date.summary: Both articles place the renewed travel/petition on New Year's Day, 1 January 2023.

location.summary: NTD describes a highway walk toward Zhengzhou; RFA separately reports a subset at the local banking-and-insurance regulator. Exact meeting point and whether these are the same physical episode are unclear.

scope.summary: Reports describe depositors arriving from several places and walking toward Zhengzhou; physical event boundaries are not established.

organizer.summary: Neither source identifies an organizer; cited social-media accounts/videos are not presumed to be organizers.

demands.summary: Reported slogans call for return of rural-bank deposits. This does not map cleanly to a listed demand category; whether the January action directly demanded state action or a public-policy change remains open.

participants_original.summary: NTD says 大批 and RFA says 不少人; neither reports an attendance count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both sources use qualitative group-size terms, but do not establish a numeric minimum; RFA also says it could not verify the videos/messages.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence is reported for the January 1 action; silence is not coded as absence.

state_response.summary: RFA relays that police took some regulator petitioners to a police station; exact status, group, and relation to the highway walk are unclear, so event-level response dimensions remain unknown.

end_date.summary: Neither report establishes when the January physical action ended.

notes: Treat as a January physical-action lead tied to the rural-bank withdrawal campaign that began in 2022; do not merge with the 2022 July protest or assume all travelers and petitioners formed one meeting. Deposit return was addressed in slogans to banks; the regulator-visit account suggests a state-facing venue but not a clearly stated public-policy demand. The reported yellow-code travel restriction is attributed and unverified.
open_questions: Were the highway march and regulator petition a single organized January 1 episode or separate arrival/petition actions?
Can a source establish a public crowd of at least 50 at a defined location?
Was a demand directed to the Chinese government/regulator, or was the direct demand solely to banks?
Can the police action at the regulator be tied to this same gathering and classified as arrest or dispersal?
What source, if any, independently verifies the yellow-code and travel-monitoring claims?
When did the physical action end?

title: Luyi residents confront fireworks-ban enforcement and overturn a police car
location: Hongdaoyuan Square, Luyi County, Zhoukou, Henan
scope: Local crowd opposing or reacting to police enforcement of the fireworks ban; source does not establish the broader campaign or event boundary.
participants_original: RFA describes a crowd/surrounding crowd; no count is published.
threshold_50_evidence: The article uses ‘crowds’ but gives no number or clearly quantified descriptor; the 50-person threshold remains pending.

start_date.summary: RFA places the Luyi gathering at about 23:00 on 2 January 2023.

location.summary: RFA identifies Hongdaoyuan Square in Luyi County, Henan.

scope.summary: The article describes a crowd reacting to fireworks-ban enforcement; it does not establish other locations as the same episode.

demands.summary: The reported trigger and confrontation concern enforcement of the fireworks ban; a precise demand is not quoted. The state-policy target is inferred from that trigger, not from a quoted slogan.

participants_original.summary: RFA says a crowd/surrounding crowd without a participant estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No numeric or clearly qualifying qualitative attendance estimate is provided; six arrests are not crowd size.

protester_violence.summary: RFA reports the crowd blocked a police car, threw drinks, damaged it, and overturned it.

state_response.summary: RFA attributes six arrests to a police statement. Other response dimensions are not established.

end_date.summary: No end time or end date for the gathering is reported.

notes: The article also mentions a crowd at a Sun Yat-sen statue in Nanjing on New Year's Eve (31 December 2022); it does not establish that this was a protest or continued into January, so it is not merged here.
open_questions: Was the crowd at Luyi at least 50 people?
What was the exact demand regarding the fireworks ban?
How long did the gathering last, and did it end through dispersal?
Was the separate Nanjing New Year's Eve crowd a protest, and did any action continue on 1 January?

title: Zhongyuan Huiji workers protest dismissals and unpaid wages
location: Zhongyuan Huiji factory, Dadukou District, Chongqing
scope: Local factory-worker protest reported at the Zhongyuan Huiji site; the source does not establish a wider coordinated episode.
organizer: Unknown; worker representatives are mentioned in negotiations, but an organizer is not identified.
participants_original: A RFA caption attributed to Reuters describes ‘hundreds’ gathered; no exact count is published.
threshold_50_evidence: The article reproduces a Reuters-attributed caption describing hundreds of workers gathered. This qualitative count exceeds 50; no numerical bounds are inferred. The Reuters article itself was not opened.

start_date.summary: RFA reports that workers protested at the factory on 7 January; 3 January is the date of dismissals, not the physical protest start.

location.summary: RFA identifies the Zhongyuan Huiji factory in Dadukou District, Chongqing.

organizer.summary: Worker representatives are mentioned in the January 8 negotiation, but no organizing body is named.

demands.summary: The account identifies sudden dismissals and disputed wages/promised bonuses involving the company and labor agencies; no explicit state-policy demand is established.

participants_original.summary: A RFA photo caption attributed to Reuters says hundreds gathered; this is qualitative, not an exact count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: ‘Hundreds’ in the Reuters-attributed caption qualitatively exceeds the threshold; the original Reuters report was not opened.

protester_violence.summary: RFA describes workers beating managers and labor-agency representatives; it separately says Reuters authenticated a worker-police clash.

state_response.summary: RFA reports district-government representatives negotiated on 7 January and worker representatives accepted a government proposal on 8 January. Negotiation is coded as accommodation, not as proof of victory.

end_date.summary: The report gives a 7 January protest and 8 January negotiation but does not establish when public gathering ended.

notes: The source's described grievances primarily name the employer and labor-dispatch agencies. Government negotiation is a response, not evidence by itself that the state or a state policy was the protest target. The crowd count is qualitative and attributed to a Reuters caption reproduced by RFA.
open_questions: Did participants explicitly demand government intervention or a policy change, or was the dispute solely with the employer and labor agencies?
Can the original Reuters report be reviewed under the source-access policy?
What was the physical gathering's end date?
Can the crowd size or protester violence be independently corroborated?

title: Yancheng First People's Hospital nurses reportedly strike over long hours and unpaid overtime
location: Yancheng First People's Hospital, Yancheng, Jiangsu; exact action site not stated.
scope: Collective workplace strike reported in one sentence; public gathering and episode boundary are not established.
participants_original: NTD reports a collective nurses' strike; no number is given.
threshold_50_evidence: The article reports a collective strike but no attendance, participant total, public meeting, or crowd count; the required 50-person public-gathering threshold is not established.

start_date.summary: NTD says nurses held a collective strike on 11 January 2023.

location.summary: The institution is named as Yancheng First People's Hospital; the action's precise physical site is not stated.

demands.summary: NTD gives long hours and unpaid overtime as the reported grievances.

participants_original.summary: The source says nurses collectively struck but supplies no number.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: A collective strike is mentioned, but the source does not establish a public meeting or 50 participants.

state_response.summary: No event-specific state response appears in the brief mention.

end_date.summary: Duration and physical end of the strike are not reported.

notes: The source is a single brief mention within an NTD roundup that relays online posts; it does not establish a public gathering, attendance, organizer, or direct demand to a state authority. The hospital is not presumed to be a state target from its name alone.
open_questions: Did a public gathering of at least 50 occur, or was this only a workplace stoppage?
What was the exact site, count, and duration?
Were demands addressed to a government body/public policy or only to the hospital employer?
Can the original video or post be identified and independently reviewed?

title: Luochuan hospital employees reportedly protest unpaid social and medical insurance
location: Gate of Luochuan County People's Hospital, Luochuan County, Yan'an, Shaanxi
scope: Hospital employees reportedly gathered at the gate over insurance contributions; affected-worker totals do not measure attendance.
organizer: NTD describes employees as self-organized; identity and organizing structure are not independently established.
participants_original: NTD describes a large group; its ‘more than 300’ figure refers to temporary workers affected by missing social insurance, not protesters.
threshold_50_evidence: The report calls the gathering a large group but gives no attendee count. The more-than-300 figure is an affected workforce, not crowd size; the 50-person threshold remains pending.

start_date.summary: NTD says the gathering at the hospital gate took place on 16 January 2023.

location.summary: NTD identifies the gate of Luochuan County People's Hospital, Shaanxi.

organizer.summary: The article describes employee self-organization, based on online video/social-media accounts, not a verified organizer identity.

demands.summary: The reported grievance concerns unpaid social insurance for temporary workers and medical insurance for staff.

participants_original.summary: NTD uses a qualitative ‘large group’ description; 300+ is the affected temporary-worker cohort, not attendance.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No crowd number is reported; do not convert affected-worker totals into protest attendance.

protester_violence.summary: The article does not report protester violence; silence is not coded as absence.

state_response.summary: NTD reports police attempting to disperse the group and shoving; an online video voice alleges police hitting people, which is not independently verified and is not coded as a confirmed beating.

end_date.summary: No physical end date or time is reported.

notes: All event details come from one NTD report relaying online video/posts without opened original material. The hospital's public status does not establish that the gathering demanded state action; the described immediate grievance is employer insurance compliance. The shouted allegation of police beating is not a verified account.
open_questions: How many people physically attended, excluding the 300+ affected-worker figure?
Did participants demand government enforcement/policy action or only hospital payment?
Was the gathering one local episode, and when did it end?
Can the original video or post be identified and reviewed?
Was force used beyond reported shoving, and were any arrests made?
